thread.title: Apple iPhone XS Preorder Concerns Overblown, Analyst Says | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple iPhone XS Preorder Concerns Overblown, Analyst Says | Investor's Business Daily
text:
News reports claiming slow first-weekend preorders for the Apple ( AAPL ) iPhone XS and XS Max have been "greatly exaggerated," a brokerage firm said Wednesday.
X Loop Capital Markets analyst Ananda Baruah said he isn't seeing evidence of weakness in early iPhone XS series sales. He reiterated his buy rating on Apple stock with a price target of 256.
Apple stock rose a fraction to 218.37 on the stock market today . It peaked at 229.67 on Sept. 5.
"It was suggested earlier this week by some of our competitors that Apple preorders could be softer than anticipated," Baruah said in a report. "We believe reports of Apple's preorder demise are greatly exaggerated."

The new handsets feature OLED displays measuring 5.8 inches and 6.5 inches, respectively. The new smartphones start at $999 and $1,099.
Apple Customers Waiting For iPhone XR Many customers are believed to be waiting for the lower priced iPhone XR. That handset has a 6.1-inch LCD screen and starts at $749. It will be available for preorder on Oct. 19 and start shipping on Oct. 26.
Analysts expect the iPhone XR to account for 50% to 55% of new iPhone shipments, Baruah said. The iPhone XS Max is seen accounting for 30% to 35% of units, with the iPhone XS making up the remaining 10% to 15%.
The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Apple staggered the launch of the new handsets so the iPhone XR wouldn't cannibalize sales of the XS series devices.
Beyond iPhone sales, Apple stock has a handful of catalysts at its back, Baruah said. They include a growing services business and share buybacks. The company also could announce a streaming video service and/or driverless car venture in the next year or two.
